event.description: Tie corresponding LayerNorm modules across the two blocks while retaining independent attention/feed-forward transforms, reversed padded operands, d=14, two heads, ff=19, rank-3 learned positions, and the 45000-step schedule.
event.proposal: Family: parameter tying. Retained incumbent is 3129 parameters at 99.190000%, a +0.190000 percentage-point margin over 99%. Same-family history: the accepted starting model used tied input/output embeddings (6080, 100.00%); the most recent failed result is attempt-0037, Q/K sharing within each attention block, an optimization failure with 11.4% peak validation; 4 prior parameter-tying candidate attempts. The immediately preceding rank-2 reversed-input attempt-0036 is an optimization failure (45000 steps, 11.1% peak validation, no checkpoint), not a scored nonqualification. Hypothesis: normalization scale/offset calibration may transfer across the two residual stages even when their attention and feed-forward computations require separate weights; tying only the two LayerNorm pairs removes 56 actual parameters (3129 to 3073). This is a parameter-tying change, not scalar pruning. It is more informative than tying the final LayerNorm to a block normalization because it preserves its distinct output-role normalization while testing the corresponding within-block mechanisms.
